bull_thesis:
The bull case is that a signed, shareholder-approved break-up closes on schedule and pays out more than the market currently marks it at. Green Dot is being dismantled into two halves under an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated 23 November 2025: Smith Ventures buys the non-bank financial-technology business for $690 million in cash, and CommerceOne Financial Corporation, a small Birmingham, Alabama bank holding company, takes Green Dot Bank into a newly listed parent (to trade on the New York Stock Exchange as CONE). Each Green Dot share converts into $8.11 in cash plus 0.2215 shares of that new company.

Four things make completion the strong base case. First, the vote is banked: at special meetings on 23 June 2026, Green Dot holders approved by 40,869,891 for against 139,918 opposed - over 99% of votes cast, roughly 72% of shares outstanding - and CommerceOne holders approved unanimously. Second, there is no financing hole. The $8.11 is funded directly out of the $690 million purchase price, which is split $155 million into the combined bank as regulatory capital, $65 million to repay debt, and $470 million to Green Dot shareholders. No lender can withdraw a commitment because there is no commitment to withdraw. Third, two independent buyers each underwrote a different half, so the price was tested twice, and the terms have not moved in the eight months since signing. Fourth, a contractual outside date of 23 November 2026 - automatically extending 90 days to 23 February 2027 if regulatory approvals remain outstanding - bounds how long capital can sit trapped.

If the deal closes and the new bank is valued anywhere near the bankers' own work, the payout is well above today's price. Citi's dividend-discount analysis, disclosed in June 2026 supplemental filings, valued the combined bank's equity at $590 million to $755 million, which implies total consideration of $15.45 to $17.51 per Green Dot share. Management's own illustrative range, given on the 24 November 2025 call, was $14.23 to $19.18. The $155 million capital injection lands inside the bank you end up owning, and the seven-year exclusive sponsor-bank agreement with the privatised fintech gives the new company a contracted revenue stream from day one rather than a standing start.

The conditions that must hold are narrow and specific: the Federal Reserve, the Alabama State Banking Department and the Utah Department of Financial Institutions all approve; the new shares list without incident; and the newly public bank finds enough natural buyers in its first weeks of trading that the forced supply from Green Dot's existing holders does not overwhelm it.
bear_thesis:
The bear case does not require the deal to break. It only requires the stock leg to be worth what the market already says it is worth - which is what makes this position unattractive at $13.16 rather than merely risky.

Only $8.11 of today's price, about 62%, is contractual cash. The other 38% is 0.2215 shares of a company that does not trade yet, cannot be hedged (there is no listed CommerceOne security to sell short), cannot be elected out of, and carries no collar, no cash election and no contingent value right. Back out the cash and the market is paying $5.05 for that stub, implying about $22.80 per new share and roughly $399 million for the entire new bank - some 32% below the low end of Citi's own valuation. That persistent discount is not inattention. Roughly 12.6 million shares, about 72% of the new company's register, are about to be handed to people who bought a Provo, Utah fintech: small-cap growth funds, payments funds, and index funds that will be mechanically deleted from Green Dot and have no mandate to hold a two-state community bank. The supply is forced and the natural buyer base has to be built from zero.

The approval risk is also real rather than procedural. Green Dot Bank operates under a Federal Reserve consent order dated 19 July 2024 carrying a $44 million civil money penalty, covering compliance risk management, unfair and deceptive practices in prepaid card marketing and servicing, and anti-money-laundering failures including inadequate disclosure of refund-processing fees between 2017 and 2022. The order required a third-party root-cause review, an outside transaction-monitoring firm and written board-oversight plans. The acquirer inheriting that problem is a bank founded in 2018 with under $1 billion of assets, buying a bank with roughly $6.65 billion of assets and $4.6 billion of deposit-type liabilities as of 31 March 2026. A much smaller acquirer absorbing a larger bank under live enforcement is exactly the profile that slows an application. The guided close has already drifted about one quarter, from an expected second quarter of 2026 at announcement to the third quarter now, and as of 28 July 2026 no Federal Reserve order has been published and no approval has been announced.

If it does break, there is no contractual backstop. Tangible book value is about $10.03 a share ($940.5 million equity less $369.0 million intangibles over roughly 57 million shares). The undisturbed price of $11.80 on 21 November 2025 is not a safe anchor either - the shares had already run from $10.56 on 18 November that same week, and that price embedded eight months of public strategic-review optionality. A failed process on a business with negative trailing return on equity of about -7.7% plausibly resolves to $10.50-$11.00, with the 52-week low of $9.31 as the overshoot. Against that, the shares at $13.16 sit about 20% above the floor and above both the 50-day ($13.06) and 200-day ($12.34) averages, having been flagged repeatedly by momentum screens through June and July 2026. You would be buying strength, not capitulation, in a name whose upside is contractually capped at the offer.
sop_bull: Event-win value: $16.00 a share (range $15.45-$17.51). Derived from the deal consideration with the stock leg marked at the bankers' valuation rather than the market's. The consideration is fixed at $8.11 cash plus 0.2215 shares of New CommerceOne. Citi's dividend-discount analysis, disclosed in the June 2026 supplemental filings, valued the combined bank's equity at $590-$755 million. Roughly 57.0 million Green Dot shares times the 0.2215 exchange ratio gives about 12.6 million new shares, and since that represents about 72% of the new company, the whole company has roughly 17.5 million shares - so Citi's range implies $33.6-$43.0 per new share, and a stub worth $7.44-$9.52. Add the $8.11 of cash and total consideration is $15.45-$17.51. Management's own illustrative range of $14.23-$19.18 (24 November 2025 call) brackets the same territory, though its top end rests on 110%-130% of projected 31 December 2029 tangible book value and is therefore a multi-year hold outcome, not a closing value. The bull SoP takes the midpoint of the banker range, $16.00, and requires the new bank to clear its listing without being swamped by forced supply.
sop_bear: Verified downside floor: $11.00 a share. This is a broken-deal value, not a contractual backstop - nothing in the merger agreement holds the price here. It is triangulated from three anchors. (1) Tangible book value of about $10.03: the 31 March 2026 balance sheet shows $940.5 million of total equity less $369.0 million of intangibles, or $571.5 million over roughly 57.0 million shares. (2) The undisturbed pre-announcement close of $11.80 on 21 November 2025 - but that figure is generous, because the shares had run from $10.56 on 18 November in the days before the news, and it embedded eight months of live strategic-review optionality that a failed process would extinguish. (3) The 52-week low of $9.31 as the sentiment overshoot. Because the standalone business is loss-making on a trailing basis (return on equity about -7.7%), the fallback is asset value rather than earnings power, which argues for the lower half of the $10.50-$11.00 band. Small offsets exist and do not move the answer: a $3.5 million reverse break fee is about $0.06 a share, and the $40 million fintech-buyer fee in certain separation-agreement terminations is about $0.70. Working floor $11.00; the board's recorded $11.80 floor is the undisturbed price and is roughly $0.80 too optimistic.
sop_breakdown: Probability-weighted across the two outcomes, because the parts here are a payout, not a business. Cash leg: $8.11 a share, contractual and funded out of Smith Ventures' $690 million purchase price ($155 million into the bank as capital, $65 million to repay debt, $470 million to shareholders) - this part carries deal risk but no financing risk. Stock leg: 0.2215 shares of New CommerceOne, marked at $6.00 for the base case, which sits above the market's own $5.05 mark (an implied $22.80 per new share) and below the $6.12 embedded in management's $14.23 low end, reflecting that first-week trading of an orphaned bank with forced sellers will likely print below the bankers' $33.6-$43.0 range. Value at close: $8.11 + $6.00 = $14.10. Value on break: $11.00. Assign an 85% chance of closing given the completed votes, absent financing condition, unchanged terms and hard outside date, against a 15% chance the Federal Reserve application stalls on Green Dot Bank's live July 2024 consent order. That gives 0.85 x $14.10 + 0.15 x $11.00 = $13.64. Sensitivity that matters: mark the stub at the market's own $5.05 instead and the base case falls to $12.84, below today's price. The entire remaining edge is a judgement on the stub's first weeks of trading, not on whether the deal closes.
risk_reward: Roughly 0.5 to 1 - the risk now exceeds the reward. From $13.16: upside to the reconciled base case of $13.60 is +3.3%; upside to management's conservative $14.23 is +8.1%; upside to the banker midpoint of $16.00 is +21.6%. Downside to the verified $11.00 floor is -16.4%; to the board's softer $11.80 reference, -10.3%. Against the $14.23 target the ratio is 0.49 to 1 on the honest floor and 0.79 to 1 on the board's floor. Note the decay: the board's recorded risk-reward of 1.56 implies an entry near $12.75, so the spread has been collected while the position sat still. The upside is contractually capped at the offer - $8.11 plus 0.2215 new shares is all a holder can ever receive - while the downside is uncapped and uncontracted. Levels that restore a two-to-one reward: below roughly $12.60 against the $11.80 reference floor, or below roughly $12.15 against the harder $11.00 floor.
catalyst_summary: A signed, shareholder-approved break-up of Green Dot paying $8.11 in cash plus 0.2215 shares of a newly listed bank holding company, guided to close in the third quarter of 2026 with a hard contractual outside date of 23 November 2026 - but at $13.16 the shares already discount the close, offering about 8% to management's conservative $14.23 against a 16% fall to an $11.00 broken-deal floor, so the asymmetry now runs the wrong way.
dated_milestone: Company-guided completion in the third quarter of 2026 (by 30 September 2026), restated in the 23 June 2026 announcement. Contractual outside date 23 November 2026, automatically extending 90 days to 23 February 2027 where required regulatory approvals remain outstanding. Shareholder approvals completed 23 June 2026. Verified as of 28 July 2026: no Federal Reserve order approving the transaction has been published and neither company has announced receipt of any of the three bank approvals; the guided window has already drifted roughly one quarter from the second quarter of 2026 expectation given at announcement.
forcing_function: Publication of the Federal Reserve Board's approval order under Section 3 of the Bank Holding Company Act, together with sign-offs from the Alabama State Banking Department and the Utah Department of Financial Institutions. That single event releases the $8.11 cash payment and triggers the New York Stock Exchange listing of New CommerceOne under the ticker CONE. Three separate Federal Reserve approvals are required: for the merger subsidiary to become a bank holding company by acquiring Green Dot Bank, for New CommerceOne to become a bank holding company by indirectly acquiring both banks, and for the merger of CommerceOne into New CommerceOne. Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust clearance and the exchange listing approval also sit in the queue. The hard boundary is the 23 November 2026 termination date, extending to 23 February 2027 if approvals are still pending. The complication is that this forcing function resolves the deal but not the valuation: the moment approval lands, the price question shifts entirely to what an orphaned community bank stub prints at in its first week of trading.
consensus_delta:
The interesting disagreement here is not between us and Wall Street - it is between the market and the company's own bankers, and the market is winning the argument.

The published sell-side and management framing says Green Dot holders are receiving $14.23 to $19.18 a share (chief financial officer, 24 November 2025), with Citi's dividend-discount work implying $15.45 to $17.51. The shares have never traded at any of those levels. They closed at $11.81 on announcement day, one cent above the prior close - the deal was worth essentially nothing to the market on the day it was struck - and eight months later, with both votes banked, they sit at $13.16, still below the floor of management's range. That is not a slow-moving market. It is a considered, persistent discount on the one part of the package nobody can observe.

Where the street assumption is factually weak is the treatment of the stock leg as though it were currency. Only $8.11 is money. The rest is 0.2215 shares of an unlisted bank, and the valuations quoted in support of the higher numbers are forward constructs: Performance Trust applied 110%-130% of projected 31 December 2029 tangible book value, and Citi used a 2.5% perpetuity growth rate against a 12.63% discount rate. Those are answers to 'what might this bank be worth in three-plus years if it executes', not 'what will 12.6 million orphaned shares fetch in week one'. Quoting $19.18 as deal proceeds is a category error, and quoting $14.23 as a target embeds an assumption that the new bank trades at $27.63 when the market currently says $22.80.

Our disagreement with the board's own catalyst entry is sharper than our disagreement with the street. That entry carried a $14.23 target against an $11.80 floor for a risk-reward of 1.56, which back-solves to an entry near $12.75. At $13.16 the identical arithmetic gives 0.79, and against a properly derived $11.00 floor it gives 0.49. The thesis has not changed; the price has, and the compensation has gone with it. A second, quieter delta: the recent buyers are momentum and value screeners (top-tier Zacks rank, 'near 52-week high' and 'attractive price-to-sales' lists through June and July 2026), not merger arbitrageurs. They are buying a fintech chart and will be handed a community bank.
valley_of_death:
There is no cash-burn hump or maturity wall here - the $65 million debt repayment out of the purchase price handles the balance sheet, and the business is improving into the close, with June-quarter earnings of $0.40 a share against a $0.30 estimate. The next three to nine months carry a different kind of risk: regulatory silence, followed by a listing.

The first hazard is the Federal Reserve application itself. Green Dot Bank has been operating under a consent order since 19 July 2024, carrying a $44 million civil money penalty for compliance risk management failures, unfair and deceptive practices in prepaid card marketing and servicing, and anti-money-laundering deficiencies including inadequate disclosure of refund-processing fees between 2017 and 2022. The remediation obligations - third-party root-cause review, outside transaction monitoring, written board-oversight plans - are still live. The Federal Reserve must now satisfy itself that CommerceOne, a bank founded in 2018 with under $1 billion of assets, has the management capacity and capital to run a $6.65 billion bank with roughly $4.6 billion of deposit-type liabilities sourced through prepaid and banking-as-a-service programmes. That is a genuine supervisory question. The guided window has already drifted one quarter, and every additional month of silence between now and the 23 November 2026 outside date will be read by the market as rising break risk, pressuring the shares toward the $11.00 floor well before any decision arrives.

The second and more probable hazard is the listing itself. Assume approval lands and the deal closes in the third or fourth quarter. Holders receive $8.11 in cash and a fractional share of a new company. There is no lock-up on a merger-consideration share, no supportive sponsor bid, no research coverage on day one, and no index membership. The stub could easily print below the $22.80 per new share the market currently implies before it finds the regional-bank buyers who would naturally own it. In that scenario the deal succeeds and the position still loses money - which is the specific way this trade goes wrong, and it does not require anything to break.
positioning_washout:
This is the most under-priced dynamic in the situation, and it runs the wrong way for a buyer at today's price.

Green Dot is currently owned as a small-cap financial-technology and payments name: index and small-cap growth funds, payments-sector specialists, and - visible in the June and July 2026 tape - momentum screeners drawn in by a top-tier Zacks rank, a price above the 200-day average of $12.34, and appearances on 'near 52-week high' and 'undervalued price-to-sales' lists. At closing, roughly 12.6 million New CommerceOne shares, about 72% of that company's register, land in those accounts. Essentially none of them can or will hold it. Index funds are mechanically deleted from Green Dot and have no mandate for a newly listed two-state bank holding company. Payments and fintech funds have no mandate either. The natural owner - a regional-bank investor - has never heard of it and has no research to read.

So the forced selling in this situation happens after the catalyst, not before it, and it falls on the asset you are left holding rather than the one you are buying. That is the inverse of the setup this funnel is built to exploit. In a classic washout you buy from distressed sellers ahead of an event; here the event hands you a security into a wave of distressed sellers.

Note also what is absent: Green Dot itself is not washed out. At $13.16 it trades above both its 50-day ($13.06) and 200-day ($12.34) averages, roughly 20% above its broken-deal floor and only 15% off its 52-week high of $15.41. There is no capitulation to buy. The only genuine capitulation on the horizon belongs to the stub, and it is worth waiting for rather than paying ahead of.
moderator_conclusion:
The event is real, binding and very likely to complete. That is not the question. The question is whether $13.16 pays you for taking it, and it does not.

What is verified: an Agreement and Plan of Merger signed 23 November 2025; shareholder approvals completed 23 June 2026 with over 99% of Green Dot votes cast in favour and CommerceOne unanimous; consideration fixed at $8.11 in cash plus 0.2215 shares of a new listed bank holding company; the cash funded from Smith Ventures' $690 million purchase price rather than from any financing commitment; no renegotiation in eight months; a contractual outside date of 23 November 2026 extending to 23 February 2027; and, as of 28 July 2026, no Federal Reserve order published and no bank approvals announced against a guided third-quarter close that has already drifted a quarter.

The reason this is a wait rather than a buy is arithmetic, not scepticism. Only 62% of the price is contractual cash. The remaining 38% is an unlisted, unhedgeable stub, and the market marks it at $5.05 - about 32% below the low end of the company's own banker's valuation. That discount is rational: at closing, roughly 12.6 million shares of a small orphaned bank get handed to fintech and index holders who cannot own it. Probability-weight the outcomes honestly - 85% chance of closing at about $14.10, 15% chance of breaking to $11.00 - and fair value is about $13.64, some 3.6% above the price. Mark the stub at the market's own number instead and fair value is $12.84, below the price. Either way the upside is capped at the offer while the downside to an $11.00 floor, which is an estimate rather than a contract, is 16%. That is roughly 0.5 to 1, and it is a material deterioration from the 1.56 recorded when this position was struck near $12.75. The spread has been collected.

The residual risk is not the one the file was opened for. It is not 'will the Federal Reserve say yes' - though Green Dot Bank's live July 2024 consent order and a sub-$1 billion acquirer taking on a $6.65 billion bank make that a real, non-procedural question. The residual risk is that the deal closes exactly as promised and the position still loses money, because an orphaned community bank stub prints below $22.80 in its first week of trading. A trade whose main failure mode is the successful outcome does not deserve fresh capital at this price.

Wait for the price, not the news. Below roughly $12.60 the reward against the $11.80 undisturbed-price reference returns to two-to-one; below roughly $12.15 it does so against the harder $11.00 floor. Either level would likely appear on the first headline of regulatory delay, which on the current drift is more likely than not. Hold what is held; do not add here.
interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Event Dossier — Green Dot Corporation (GDOT)
### Event-driven special situation: the CommerceOne / Smith Ventures break-up
Prepared 28 July 2026. Last traded price **$13.16** (close of 27 July 2026, NYSE).
Built from SEC filings (8-K, DEFM14A, Form 425), company releases, Federal Reserve
enforcement records and market data. No earnings-call transcript bundle was available for
this run, so the usual transcript sections are answered against the deal record instead, and
no management quotation appears here unless sourced to a specific dated document.

---

## 1. WHAT THE EVENT ACTUALLY IS

Green Dot is not being bought whole. On 23 November 2025 the company signed an agreement to
split itself in two and sell each half to a different buyer:

- **CommerceOne Financial Corporation**, a privately held bank holding company in Birmingham,
  Alabama (its subsidiary CommerceOne Bank was founded in 2018 and held roughly **$892 million**
  in total assets across two locations with 59 employees as of March 2026), takes Green Dot
  Bank. The two banks are then placed under a brand new, publicly traded parent — "New
  CommerceOne" — which intends to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CONE.
- **Smith Ventures, LLC** buys Green Dot's non-bank financial-technology operations and takes
  them private, to be run as an independent company. The privatised fintech signs a
  **seven-year exclusive sponsor-bank agreement** with the new bank, which is what lets both
  halves function apart.

For every Green Dot share you hold at closing you receive a fixed package: **$8.11 in cash
plus 0.2215 shares of New CommerceOne**. Former Green Dot holders end up owning roughly 72%
of the new bank company.

**Where the cash comes from matters, and it is good news.** Smith Ventures pays **$690 million
in cash** for the fintech. That sum is carved up as follows: **$155 million** injected into the
combined bank to bolster liquidity and regulatory capital, **$65 million** to repay existing
debt, and the remaining **$470 million** distributed to Green Dot shareholders — which, over
roughly 57 million shares, is the $8.11. The cash leg is therefore funded out of a purchase
price, not out of a financing commitment that a lender could pull.

That second half of the package is the whole argument, and it is worth stating plainly at the
top: **this is not a cash deal.** Only about 62% of the value at today's price is contractual
cash. The rest is stock in a company that does not yet trade, whose price nobody can observe,
and whose first day of trading is the moment the value is actually set.

---

## 2. IS THE CATALYST REAL, DATED, AND BINDING?

**Real and binding: yes, on strong evidence.**

| Test | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Signed agreement | Agreement and Plan of Merger, 23 Nov 2025, unanimously approved by the Green Dot board | Binding |
| Shareholder approval | Special meetings held **23 June 2026**. Green Dot: 40,869,891 for / 139,918 against / 52,234 abstaining — over 99% of votes cast, about 72% of shares outstanding. CommerceOne: 100% in favour, about 69% of outstanding | Cleared, and not close |
| Financing condition | None disclosed in the merger proxy; the cash comes from the $690M purchase price | No financing hole |
| Two independent buyers | A bank buyer and a separate fintech buyer, each wanting a different half | Two parties had to underwrite the price; harder to walk |
| Break fees | Green Dot pays CommerceOne $27.0M on specified terminations; CommerceOne pays Green Dot $3.5M in reverse; the fintech buyer pays Green Dot $40.0M if the separation agreement terminates in certain cases | The asymmetry (Green Dot's is nearly eight times the reverse fee) says Green Dot is the more motivated seller |

**Dated: partly.** There is no single hard calendar date on which the deal is guaranteed to
complete. What exists is:

- A **company-guided window** — "expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2026,"
  repeated in the 23 June 2026 announcement. A quarter, not a date.
- A **contractual outside date** — the merger agreement terminates on **23 November 2026**,
  automatically extendable by 90 days to **23 February 2027** where required regulatory
  approvals are still outstanding. That is the hard boundary: nine weeks away at the guided
  pace, seven months at the outside.

So the correct description is a binding contract with a soft target inside a hard contractual
boundary. That is stronger than a management aspiration and weaker than a regulator's
scheduled decision date.

**One qualifier the board's catalyst entry does not capture: the window has already drifted.**
At announcement the companies pointed to four-to-six months for approvals, and contemporaneous
trade coverage carried an expected close "during the second quarter of 2026." The guidance now
reads third quarter. That is roughly one quarter of slippage — unremarkable for a bank
application, but it is drift, not adherence, and it should be priced as such.

---

## 3. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT TO CLEAR

Everything discretionary that remains sits with bank regulators:

1. **Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System** — approval under Section 3 of the Bank
   Holding Company Act, in three separate pieces: for the merger subsidiary to become a bank
   holding company by acquiring Green Dot Bank; for New CommerceOne to become a bank holding
   company by indirectly acquiring both banks; and for the merger of CommerceOne into New
   CommerceOne.
2. **Alabama State Banking Department** (CommerceOne Bank's home regulator).
3. **Utah Department of Financial Institutions** (Green Dot Bank's home regulator).
4. Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust clearance and NYSE listing approval for the new shares.

**Verification as of 28 July 2026: no Federal Reserve order approving this transaction has been
published, and neither company has announced receipt of any of the three bank approvals.** The
most recent transaction news of any kind remains the 23 June 2026 shareholder-vote
announcement; company news since then has been operating items (an Everest Group earned-wage-
access ranking on 27 July, a Treasury Prime cash-network partnership on 25 June). The catalyst
has **not fired**, and it has **not been abandoned** — it is sitting in the regulators'
in-trays with roughly nine weeks left in the guided quarter.

---

## 4. HOW CREDIBLE IS THE SPONSOR ON HITTING IT?

Four observations, none of them fatal, all of them worth pricing.

- **Green Dot's own credibility is the weak leg.** The company put itself up for strategic
  review in early 2025 after a severe de-rating; the reference "unaffected" price the bankers
  used was about **$7.45 (7 March 2025)**. It is selling because the standalone business
  stopped working, not from strength. Trailing-twelve-month results show a net loss — return on
  equity of about **−7.7%** and a negative earnings yield — against a positive but modest
  operating return on assets of about 0.4%. Management is a motivated seller, which helps
  completion and hurts negotiating leverage. The board has also granted the chief executive a
  bonus explicitly tied to completing the merger: alignment with closing, but also a reminder
  that the people quoting you a $14.23 value are paid to get it done.
- **CommerceOne is small and private, buying something much larger than itself.** A bank
  founded in 2018 in Birmingham, with under $1 billion of assets, is taking on Green Dot Bank,
  whose balance sheet carried about **$6.65 billion of assets at 31 March 2026** — roughly
  $4.6 billion of that in customer deposit-type liabilities. Regulators will look hard at
  management capacity, capital, and the compliance record of a bank whose deposits arrive
  through prepaid and banking-as-a-service programmes.
- **Green Dot Bank is not a clean applicant, and the prior read of this file missed it.** On
  **19 July 2024** the Federal Reserve Board issued a consent order against Green Dot
  Corporation and Green Dot Bank carrying a **$44 million civil money penalty**. The findings
  covered compliance risk management, unfair and deceptive practices in the marketing, selling
  and servicing of prepaid debit cards, and anti-money-laundering failures — including
  inadequate disclosure of refund-processing fees in tax-refund services between 2017 and 2022.
  The order compelled a third-party root-cause review, an outside transaction-monitoring firm,
  and written board-oversight and improvement plans. **A bank under a live enforcement action
  is exactly the profile that slows a Federal Reserve application**, because the regulator must
  satisfy itself that a much smaller acquirer can manage the problem it is inheriting. This is
  the single most likely cause of further delay, and the tail where the deal actually fails.
- **No one has wobbled.** Both boards recommended it, both shareholder bases voted for it
  overwhelmingly, no party has sought to renegotiate, and the terms are unchanged from November
  2025 through the June 2026 vote. Operationally the business is improving into the close —
  **June-quarter earnings of $0.40 a share beat the $0.30 estimate**, and 2025 revenue grew
  about 21% (though net income fell about 270% into a loss over the same year).

---

## 5. THE DOWNSIDE FLOOR — WHAT ACTUALLY BACKSTOPS THE PRICE

If the deal fails, what is a Green Dot share worth? Three verified anchors:

| Anchor | Value per share | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tangible book value (equity less intangibles) | **about $10.03** | Q1 2026 balance sheet: $940.5M total equity less $369.0M of intangibles = $571.5M, over roughly 57.0M shares |
| Undisturbed market price before the deal | **$11.80** | Closing price on 21 November 2025, the last trading day before announcement |
| Fifty-two-week low | **$9.31** | Trailing twelve months |

The honest floor sits between the first two, not at the top of them. The $11.80 undisturbed
price already contained eight months of public strategic-review optionality — that price was
itself partly a bet that a deal would happen, and the shares had run from **$10.56 on
18 November to $11.80 on 21 November**, the trading week before the news. Strip the deal
expectation out after a failed process, add a trailing-twelve-month net loss, and a broken deal
plausibly resolves toward **$10.50 to $11.00**, with $9.31 as the overshoot if sentiment runs.
Small offsets exist: a $3.5 million reverse fee (about $0.06 a share) or, in the
separation-agreement scenarios, $40 million from the fintech buyer (about $0.70 a share).
Neither changes the picture.

**Working floor: $11.00.** It is real in the sense that tangible book and a regulated deposit
franchise sit underneath it. It is **not** a hard floor in the sense a cash-tender arbitrage
enjoys — nothing contractual holds the price there, there is no cash election, no collar, and
no contingent value right.

The uncomfortable arithmetic: the shares trade at **$13.16, about 20% above that floor**. There
is no margin of safety in the price today. You are paid for the deal closing, and only for that.

---

## 6. THE PART EVERYONE UNDER-PRICES: THE STOCK LEG

This is where the real work is, and where the received "$14.23 target" falls apart under
inspection.

The often-quoted $14.23 is the **bottom** of management's own illustrative range of **$14.23 to
$19.18** per share, given by the chief financial officer on the 24 November 2025 call. The top
of that range is not a closing value at all: the supporting work applied **110% to 130% of
projected 31 December 2029 tangible book value** (Performance Trust) and a dividend-discount
model at a 2.5% perpetuity growth rate and a 12.63% discount rate producing a $1,160 million
undiscounted terminal value (Citi). Treating $19.18 as deal proceeds is a category error — it
is what the stub might be worth after three or more years of successful bank operation.

Separately, in supplemental disclosures issued in June 2026 (prompted by three disclosure
lawsuits — Phillips, 27 May 2026; Richardson, 28 May 2026; Zaccagnino, 8 June 2026, all in New
York state courts, all disclosure-only claims the companies call meritless), Citi's
dividend-discount analysis put the combined company's equity value at **$590 million to $755
million**, implying total consideration of **$15.45 to $17.51** per Green Dot share.

Work the arithmetic back. About 57.0 million Green Dot shares times the 0.2215 exchange ratio
produces roughly 12.6 million New CommerceOne shares, and if that is 72% of the new company,
the whole company has about 17.5 million shares. Citi's $590–755 million therefore implies
**$33.6 to $43.0** per New CommerceOne share.

Now read the tape. At **$13.16**, after subtracting the $8.11 of contractual cash, the market is
paying **$5.05 for 0.2215 shares — an implied $22.80 per New CommerceOne share, or roughly
$399 million for the whole new bank.** That is about **32% below the low end of the banker's own
valuation**, and 17% below the stub value embedded in management's own $14.23 floor.

Some of that gap is ordinary deal risk and the time value of waiting. Most of it is not. Most of
it is the market saying, correctly in my view, that **the day this thing lists is the day it gets
sold.** Roughly 72% of the register of a brand-new, thinly covered, $400–750 million
Alabama-and-Utah bank holding company is about to be handed to people who bought a Provo, Utah
financial-technology company: small-cap growth funds, payments-sector funds, and index funds
that will be mechanically deleted from Green Dot and have no mandate to hold CONE. None of them
chose a community bank. The supply is forced and the natural buyer base — regional bank
investors — has to be built from zero.

So the load-bearing uncertainty in this trade is not "will the Federal Reserve say yes." It is
**"what does an orphaned bank stub print at when 12.6 million shares come looking for a bid in
week one."**

---

## 7. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**Concerning**
- **The reward is now smaller than the risk, and it has decayed since we entered.** Working
  backwards from the board's recorded risk-reward of 1.56 against a $14.23 target and an $11.80
  floor implies an entry near **$12.75**. At today's $13.16 the same arithmetic gives **0.79**.
  Against the more honest $11.00 floor it is roughly **0.49**. The spread has been collected
  while the position sat still.
- Only 62% of today's price is contractual cash; 38% is an unobservable stock leg whose value
  will be set by forced sellers, cannot be hedged (there is no listed CommerceOne security to
  sell short), and cannot be elected out of.
- Green Dot Bank operates under a live July 2024 Federal Reserve consent order; the pending
  approval is not a formality.
- The guided close has already drifted roughly one quarter, from the second quarter of 2026 to
  the third.
- The shares are not washed out. At $13.16 they sit above both the 50-day ($13.06) and 200-day
  ($12.34) averages, and the stock has been repeatedly flagged by momentum and value screens
  through June and July 2026. You are buying strength, not capitulation — an unusual and
  unwelcome starting point for a special situation.
- The standalone franchise is loss-making on a trailing basis, so the fallback is asset value,
  not earnings power.
- Green Dot's $27.0 million break fee is nearly eight times CommerceOne's reverse fee, which
  tells you which side wanted this more.

**Reassuring**
- The vote is done and it was not close: over 99% of votes cast.
- No financing condition — the $8.11 is funded from the $690 million purchase price, and a
  further $155 million of that price goes in as bank capital, which strengthens the stub you
  receive.
- Terms unchanged for eight months; no renegotiation, no wobble.
- Two separate buyers each wanted a different half, so both pieces were independently
  underwritten.

  long capital can be trapped.
- The litigation is the standard disclosure-only variety, already answered with supplemental
  filings, with no injunction sought or granted.
- The operating business is beating expectations into the close.

---

## 8. VERDICT FOR THE DIRECTOR

The event is genuine, documented, shareholder-approved and unconditional on financing.
Credibility of the **event** is high. What is low is the **compensation for taking it**, and the
reason is that the market has already done the work: the shares have drifted up toward the
cash-plus-discounted-stub value, so the remaining spread of roughly 8% to management's own
conservative $14.23 is being offered against a 16–20% fall to a floor that is an estimate rather
than a contract.

Run the expectation honestly. Give the deal an 85% chance of closing. Mark the stub at $6.00 —
above the market's $5.05, below management's $6.12 — for a closing value near $14.10. Value a
broken deal at $11.00. The probability-weighted result is about **$13.64**, roughly 3.6% above
today's price. Mark the stub at the market's own $5.05 instead and the expectation falls to
**$12.84**, below today's price. The entire remaining edge in this position is a judgement about
the first-week trading of an orphaned community bank.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing: you are not buying a defined-risk cash arbitrage —
you are buying $8.11 of cash and a pre-listing position in a small orphaned bank, at a price
that already assumes the deal closes.** Size it as a stub-equity bet with deal risk attached,
never as a cash spread. If the position is to be added to, the level that restores a two-to-one
reward against the $11.80 reference floor is **below roughly $12.60**; against the harder $11.00
floor, below roughly $12.15.

The moat question is close to moot, and the honest answer is unflattering: the franchise is
being dismantled precisely because prepaid and banking-as-a-service economics have been ground
down by payment-app, neobank and stablecoin competition — a structural force, not a cycle. The
bank charter retains scarcity value, which is exactly why it found a buyer, but a licence you
can sell is not the same thing as an earnings moat, and negative returns on equity alongside 21%
revenue growth is the signature of a franchise that was losing, not compounding.

interrogator_dossier:
# Green Dot Corporation (GDOT) — Event Dossier

**Setup type:** Merger arbitrage / deal completion. This is a special situation, not a quality compounder. The thesis is the spread between today's price (about $13.36 as of June 26, 2026) and the agreed deal value (roughly $14.23 per share), gated on one remaining event: bank regulators signing off so the transaction can close.

## 1. THE EVENT — is it real, dated, and binding?

It is real and largely locked. On November 23, 2025, Green Dot announced a strategic break-up: CommerceOne Financial will acquire Green Dot Bank and roll it into a new, publicly traded bank holding company, while Smith Ventures buys and takes private Green Dot's non-bank financial-technology operations. The two pieces are wired together — the new bank becomes the fintech's exclusive issuing bank.

The terms are fixed (this is what makes it arbitrage rather than open-ended speculation): each Green Dot share converts into **$8.11 in cash plus 0.2215 shares of the new CommerceOne holding company**. The cash piece alone is $8.11; the stock piece carries the rest of the value.

The deal has cleared the biggest discretionary hurdle. On **June 23, 2026**, both Green Dot and CommerceOne shareholders voted to approve, with 99% of Green Dot shares voted in favor — about 72% of all shares outstanding. A definitive proxy (DEFM14A) and the new entity's registration (Form 424B3, filed by Compass Sub North) are on file with the SEC.

What is left is the regulatory close, expected in the **third quarter of 2026**. The pending approvals are the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, the Alabama State Banking Department, and the Utah Department of Financial Institutions — the standard package for a bank-holding-company change of control. There is no longer a financing contingency or a shareholder-vote risk; the catalyst is a dated, binding regulatory clearance, not a soft promise.

## 2. CREDIBILITY OF THE PARTIES

Credibility here is about deal certainty, not management's operating skill (the operating franchise is being dismantled and sold, so its quality no longer carries the thesis). The relevant questions are whether regulators will approve and whether the parties stay committed.

Positives: the shareholder vote is done and overwhelming; the structure is conventional (a bank holding company buying a chartered bank, with the fintech carved out to a private buyer); both companies have signed, filed, and publicly reaffirmed the Q3 2026 timeline. Bank deals of this size routinely clear the Fed and state regulators when there are no obvious antitrust or safety-and-soundness red flags, and a roughly $1.1B fintech/community-bank tie-up is not the kind of deal that draws a heavy-handed second look.

Risks: bank-regulatory approval is genuinely discretionary and can slip. The Fed has been slower and more demanding on bank M&A in recent years, and any one of three regulators can extend the timeline. There is also a Scott+Scott "investigation" notice circulating — these are routine plaintiff-firm solicitations on announced deals and almost never derail a transaction shareholders have already approved, but they are worth noting as background noise rather than a real obstacle.

## 3. THE FLOOR — what backstops the price if the event fails?

The downside is bounded but not bulletproof. The $8.11 cash component is contractual and large relative to the share price, which anchors a meaningful chunk of value. The verified downside floor used here is about $11.80 — roughly where the stock would settle on a deal break, reflecting Green Dot's standalone value as a still-cash-generative (if structurally challenged) fintech-plus-bank, supported by the cash on the balance sheet and the businesses that were independently bid for. That floor is below today's price, so a break would hurt, but the cash component and the fact that two separate buyers wanted the pieces limit how far it can fall. The 52-week low was $9.31, set before the deal momentum, which marks a realistic worst-case stress level if the deal collapsed and sentiment overshot.

## 4. THE ASYMMETRY

- Live price: about $13.36
- Deal value target: about $14.23 (cash plus the value of the 0.2215 stock piece)
- Downside floor on a break: about $11.80

That is roughly $0.87 of upside to the target against $1.56 of downside to the floor from current levels — a spread reward-to-risk near 1.6 to 1, with the key sweetener being that the hard work (shareholder approval) is already behind it and only a dated regulatory clearance remains. The asymmetry is modest in absolute terms because the spread has already tightened as the deal de-risked; this is a late-stage arb, not a wide-open mispricing.

## 5. RED / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Shareholder vote passed overwhelmingly (June 23, 2026) — the single largest deal risk is retired.
🟢 Fixed terms, definitive filings on record, cash component is large and contractual.
🟢 Dated close (Q3 2026) with a conventional, approvable structure.
🔴 Three separate bank regulators must still approve; bank-M&A timelines can slip a quarter or more.
🔴 The stock-component value floats with the new CommerceOne entity, so the realized payout is not perfectly fixed.
🔴 Spread is already thin (~6-7%), so most of the easy money is gone; downside to the break floor exceeds upside to the target.

## 6. VERDICT FOR THE DIRECTOR

This is a clean, late-stage merger arbitrage with the vote already won and only regulatory clearance outstanding into Q3 2026. The catalyst is real, dated, and binding, and the floor is reasonable thanks to the cash component — but the spread has compressed enough that the reward-to-risk is only mildly favorable. Size it as a defined-risk arb position, not a high-conviction asymmetric swing.

# GDOT — Green Dot Corp — Interrogator Dossier (Event-Driven / Merger-Arb)

**Frame:** This is NOT a business-quality or compounding judgment. Green Dot is a structurally-pressured prepaid-card / BaaS issuer with a thin, eroding standalone franchise. The thesis is the SPREAD between the live price (~$12.80, 2026-06-22) and the event-resolved deal value, gated on the merger firing, with a defined cash floor that bounds the loss. The catalyst carries the thesis.

## 1. THE EVENT — is it real, dated, binding?

**Real and binding.** On 2026-11-23 Green Dot announced definitive agreements (Merger Agreement + Separation Agreement) under which: CommerceOne Financial Corp. acquires Green Dot and combines Green Dot Bank into a new publicly-traded bank holding company (NewCo); Smith Ventures LLC simultaneously acquires the fintech/embedded-finance business from NewCo for $690M cash. Per-share consideration: $8.11 cash + 0.2215 shares of NewCo. Former GDOT holders own ~72% of NewCo, CommerceOne ~28%. Aggregate value $825M-$1.1B (incl. ~$470M cash). Management-stated implied per-share value range: $14.23 (low TBV multiple) - $19.18 (high) at close.

**Dated and imminent.** DEFM14A filed 2026-05-08. Special meeting / shareholder vote 2026-06-23 (tomorrow). Expected close Q2-2026 (by ~06-30), contingent on final regulatory sign-off.

**Conditions:** shareholder approval (both special meetings 06-23), required bank regulatory approvals (Fed/OCC/state — a BHC formation, so the regulatory step is the genuine residual risk, not antitrust), and customary closing conditions.

## 2. THE VERIFIED DOWNSIDE FLOOR

The floor is NOT the $8.11 cash alone, because ~22% of consideration is unlisted NewCo stock. Cash leg $8.11 is contractually fixed/hard. Stock leg 0.2215 x NewCo marked conservatively floors the blended DEAL value at management's low-end $14.23. A break floor (deal fails, GDOT reverts standalone) sits near the recent unaffected / 50-day-low zone ~$11.55-$11.80 (52-wk low $9.31 is the tail). Working downside floor for the held seat: ~$11.80 — deal-break reversion, comfortably below live $12.80 and well below the $14.23 low-end deal value. Bounds loss at roughly -8% vs upside-to-low-end +11% ($14.23) and up to +50% ($19.18) on a high-end NewCo re-rate.

## 3. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

RED — Stock-component risk: ~22% of consideration is 0.2215 shares of an unlisted NewCo BHC; post-close liquidity, realized TBV multiple, and combined credit/deposit profile unknown. The 'target' is the LOW end of management's own range; do not credit $19.18 as base.
RED — Bank-regulatory gate: requires Fed/OCC/state approval to FORM a new BHC; the one condition that can slip past Q2 (SOFT-extension risk), though no slippage announced.
YELLOW — Strike-suit overhang (benign): three NY disclosure-deficiency suits (Phillips 05-27, Richardson 05-28, Zaccagnino 06-08) + Schall/Wohl & Fruchter/Kaskela investigations. Company already issued supplemental merger disclosures — textbook moot-the-claim pattern; no injunction sought/granted.
GREEN — No financing condition of note on the cash leg; binding gate is regulatory + vote, both imminent.
GREEN — Standalone fundamentals stable not collapsing: Q1-26 rev +17% YoY to $656.2M, NI +109% YoY to $53.7M, EPS beat $0.30 — supports the break-floor near unaffected levels.
GREEN — Trading BELOW low-end deal value, not through terms: live $12.80 < $14.23 — a genuine arb discount (PENDING_HARD), not an ARB name at/through the offer.

## 4. SPREAD ECONOMICS

Live $12.80 (2026-06-22, intraday $12.76-$12.92). Target (low-end deal value, base) $14.23 -> +11.2% gross, captured on close. Floor (break/standalone) ~$11.80 -> -7.8%. Asymmetry ~1.4-1.6:1 to low-end target; 3-6:1 if NewCo re-rates toward $19.18. Catalyst PENDING_HARD: dated (vote 06-23, close Q2-26), binding (definitive agreements), real asymmetry, defined floor.

## 5. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

EVENT-DRIVEN / DEAL-COMPLETION, not a franchise judgment. Single most important thing to weigh: the stock-component + bank-regulatory tail — the $8.11 cash leg is hard, but ~22% of value rides on an unlisted NewCo whose mark sets whether realized value lands at $14.23 or $19.18, and the Fed/OCC formation approval is the one gate that could slip. The 06-23 vote is near-certain (board-recommended, no competing bid/activist no-vote); strike-suits are mooted noise. Clean held-seat arb, catalyst imminent, live price below low-end resolved value. Moat NONE (commoditized prepaid/BaaS, payments-disintermediation-exposed) but irrelevant; the catalyst carries the thesis. Secular threat manageable for the event value. Trajectory STABLE.

skeptic_kill_fact: The bull's load-bearing claim — live ~$12.80 sits BELOW a 'resolved' deal value of $14.23, delivering +11% on close in days-to-weeks — is false. Only $8.11 of the consideration is hard cash; the other ~$6.12/sh is 0.2215 shares of an UNLISTED, never-traded NewCo bank holding company. Per Citi's fairness opinion (DEFM14A / Form 425), $14.23-$19.18 is an ILLUSTRATIVE range that credits that stub at 1.00x-1.81x tangible book; NewCo pro-forma TBV is only ~$490M (~$355M / ~$6.12 per GDOT share to former holders). The $14.23 'conservative low end' is NOT conservative — it marks a brand-new small-cap bank (born of a forced restructuring of a payments-disintermediation-exposed prepaid/BaaS issuer, with admitted forced index/mandate selling at the open) at FULL 1.00x book. At a realistic newly-listed-bank discount (~0.7-0.8x TBV) the stub is worth ~$3.7-4.9 and realized value is ~$11.8-$13.0 — i.e. the market's $12.80 IS the correct mark, not an arb discount. There is no genuine spread to capture; the stock is at fair, not below it. Compounding this: the bull's 'close by ~06-30, days-to-weeks' timeline is wrong — the 06-23 vote only clears the SHAREHOLDER condition, while the binding gate (Fed / Utah DFI / ASBD approval to FORM a new BHC) is multi-month; the merger agreement's outside date is Nov 23, 2026 PLUS a 90-day auto-extension. Single-binary stub with no hard floor (on a break the holder owns standalone no-moat equity, not the $8.11 cash), trading-through on a mark-to-model unlisted share. Default REFUTED stands.
